title: Tenali Raman and the Two Golden Statues

full_text:
A master goldsmith from Tanjore presented King Krishnadevaraya with two magnificent statues of celestial maidens, each three feet high, cast in solid gold. Both statues had the same weight, the same exquisite smile, and identical craftsmanship.
The goldsmith announced:
'Your Majesty, one statue is worth five thousand gold coins, but the other statue is worth fifty thousand gold coins!
Whosoever can explain the difference without cutting the gold shall receive my master's blessing!'

The court goldsmiths scratched their heads; the scales showed identical weight, and the metal was pure gold in both.
The King turned to Tenali Raman.

Tenali asked for a long, thin, flexible strand of golden wire.
He approached the first statue and found a small hole in its right ear.
He pushed the wire into the ear: the wire traveled through the head and came out through the statue’s open mouth!

Tenali explained:
'Maharaj, this statue represents the untrustworthy gossip.
Whatever secret is confided into his ear immediately spills out through his mouth to cause misery, broken families, and political chaos.
Gold spent on a gossip brings only trouble; this statue is worth the lesser sum.'

Tenali then took the wire and inserted it into the ear of the second statue.
The wire entered, curved downwards into the statue's hollow chest, and remained securely within its golden heart, never emerging from mouth or ear!

Tenali bowed with deep reverence:
'This second statue, Maharaj, represents the true friend, the honorable minister, and the faithful guardian.
Whatever secret, sorrow, or confession is entrusted to his ear is locked forever in the quiet sanctuary of his heart.
He guards confidences with his life, speaks only to heal, and remains steadfast through all trials.
A loyal friend is worth more than fifty thousand gold coins—he is beyond all earthly price!'

The goldsmith bowed low in tears of admiration:
'Tenali Raman, thou hast understood the soul of my art!'
King Krishnadevaraya embraced Tenali, placing the second golden statue in the royal council chamber as an eternal reminder of ministerial integrity.
moral: External appearances cannot reveal virtue; true character is shown by how one receives and handles confidences.

Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
